one_month_reasoning: Q3 2026 results are the main scheduled event. Uber IR had not posted a date as of 2026-10-05, but date aggregators list Nov 3 before the open, and Q3'25 was Nov 4 (src 10). So I now put ~85% on the print falling inside the window, up from ~75%. Guide: GB $58.25-60.25B, non-GAAP EPS $0.84-0.88 (src 1,4). The print will be the first since the Sep 2 cut of ~3,300 corporate jobs (~10% of staff, src 16). The CEO said the savings will be reinvested in lower prices and growth rather than dropped to margin (src 16), so expect GAAP restructuring charges and possibly a cautious margin guide. Other swing factors: the Q4 guide, buyback restart timing, and any AV P&L sizing. Two-sided: Q2 beat but traded -5%. The Delivery Hero acceptance period ends Nov 5, just outside the window. Uber's own stake is ~24.8% direct + ~11.7% derivatives, and Prosus's irrevocable ~17% takes it to ~53% (src 7), so the 50%+1 minimum is very likely met. Insider buying near spot (CEO $10.0M at $70.96, COO $5.3M at ~$75.8; Form 4s) offsets negative 12-month momentum. Net: symmetric, median ~$69.8, log-sd 0.11 (35%/3.5 = 10%, widened for the print).

fair_value.method: Blend of 45% P/E (18x, the core-peer NTM median, on ~$4.70 NTM EPS at horizon = $84.6), 35% SBC-adjusted FCF yield (7.5% on ~$5.80/share = $77.3) and 20% EV/EBITDA (9.5x, the NTM peer median, on ~$15.0B = $72). Comps are restated on a consistent NTM basis, and the FCF yield is held at today's level, so no re-rating is assumed. The result is ~$79.5.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM (Q4'27-Q3'28) non-GAAP EPS ~$4.70 (14% below consensus blend) x 18x (core-peer NTM median ~18x)

inputs_detail.derivation: 0.72+0.81+0.86 plus Q4 ~$0.93 (Q3 midpoint +8% seq., in line with the Q2->Q3 step). +35% vs FY25, matching 28-44% YoY quarterly growth. Non-GAAP EPS here is burdened by SBC: Adj. EBITDA minus non-GAAP op. income (~$0.6-0.7B/qtr) equals D&A plus SBC (src 1,5). Cross-check vs consensus: MarketScreener FY27 EPS $4.53 / FY28 $5.79 (src 15). My FY27 $4.15 / FY28 $4.98 are ~8-14% below it, which is the haircut for the AV/DH drag. The Sep 2026 layoffs (src 16) are a potential offset that I do not add, because management said the savings get reinvested in price.

Bookings growing 18-22% cc (guide) with incremental margin expansion (non-GAAP op. margin 3.7% of GB, +40bp YoY), ~3-4% annual net share-count decline (diluted shares -4% YoY), and CA insurance savings from 2027 (src 4). Consensus 3Y EPS CAGR is ~31% (src 13) and FY27 consensus EPS $4.56 (src 12, may mix GAAP). I haircut both for AV investment P&L drag the CFO said will come (src 3). FY27 ~$4.15, FY28 ~$4.98. Consensus-blend equivalent is ~$5.48 (0.25x4.53+0.75x5.79, src 15), so $4.70 is ~14% below it. [Citation gate 2026-10-07] The TIKR page (src 12) does not show a FY27 consensus of $4.56; current FY27 consensus is $4.54 (MarketScreener, src 15) or $4.43 (S&P Global via https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/uber/forecast/ page data). 3Y EPS growth 31.04% confirmed (src 13).

Restated on one NTM consensus basis (0.25xFY26E+0.75xFY27E, MarketScreener, prices as of 2026-10-05; src 15). Peer median NTM P/E ~19.6x across 10 peers, ~18.0x for the core 7. UBER today is 16.6x on the same basis. 18x sits at the core median and below the all-peer median, so it implies a small re-rate from 16.6x. I keep it because the multiple is applied to my EPS, ~14% below consensus, so on consensus EPS it is ~15.4x. The discount to the 19.6x median reflects the verified Waymo own-app risk (Austin/Atlanta Jan 2028) and the unsized $10B AV program (src 3). [Citation gate 2026-10-07] [Citation gate 2026-10-07] Peer medians cited here are superseded by filings-based values: P/E 16.6x (core-7 13.3x), EV/EBITDA 9.2x (core-7 7.9x, range 4.8x TCOM to 18.6x MELI); UBER 16.7x P/E and 11.3x EV/EBITDA at the $69.48 Oct-5 close. The multiple chosen here is the agent's judgment and is unchanged.

Peer median fwd P/E is 26.0x (range 8.0x-209x, 11 peers). Uber trades at 16.8x fwd today (src 13). 18x is inside the range and near CART/GRAB (17.7x/18.2x), above mature travel (BKNG 14.3x, EXPE 11.7x), well below DASH 28x. The discount to the median reflects robotaxi disintermediation risk that won't resolve before 2028 (src 3, 11). [Citation gate 2026-10-07] This round-1 entry quotes stockanalysis page-printed forward P/Es (aggregator multiples, mixed GAAP/adjusted basis) and a 26.0x median that the agent withdrew in round 2; it does not feed the 18x.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: NTM FCF ~$13.8B less SBC ~$2.3B = $11.5B / ~1.98B diluted shares = ~$5.80; at 7.5% yield (about today's forward SBC-adjusted yield, no re-rating)

inputs_detail.derivation: TTM $10.1B grown ~18-20%/yr (in line with EPS/EBITDA growth of 33% slowing). FY27 ~$12.3B, FY28 ~$14.3B, blended NTM ~$13.8B. AV equity and fleet support sits mostly in investing cash flow (src 3). Below the consensus blend of ~$14.7B (FY27 $13.7B / FY28 $15.0B, src 15). [Citation gate 2026-10-07] MarketScreener (src 15, estimates last updated 2026-02-04) shows FY27 FCF $13,082M and FY28 $14,961M, so the consensus blend is ~$14.5B (not $14.7B from $13.7B/$15.0B). The agent's ~$13.8B estimate is unchanged.
2.050B diluted Q2'26 (src 1), 2.043B outstanding Jul 31 (src 2). ~50% of FCF to buybacks (src 3) is ~$5-6B/yr, retiring ~75M shares at ~$75, less SBC issuance. ~$16B authorization remains (src 4).

Revised from 7%. Today's forward SBC-adjusted FCF yield: market cap ~$142.7B ($69.62 x 2.05B, src 1). Forward FCF ~$12.9B (0.25x$10.5B FY26E + 0.75x$13.7B FY27E, src 15) less ~$2.1B SBC (src 4) = ~$10.8B, a ~7.6% yield. The supervisor showed Uber is roughly fairly valued against NTM peers, with no EBITDA re-rating support. Applying 7% to horizon-year FCF therefore baked in re-rating on top of two years of growth, which double-counted the upside. 7.5% holds today's yield, so value comes only from FCF growth and buybacks. [Citation gate 2026-10-07] Corrected inputs: Oct-5 close $69.48 x 2.043B shares = $141.9B; forward FCF $12.43B (0.25 x $10.49B + 0.75 x $13.08B, src 15) less $2.03B SBC (guide midpoint, src 4) = $10.41B, a 7.3% yield (not $142.7B / $12.9B / 7.6%). The 7.5% judgment is unchanged.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: NTM adj. EBITDA at horizon ~$15.0B x 9.5x = EV ~$142.5B; ~zero net debt ex-DH; / ~1.98B shares = ~$72

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus FY27 $13.8B / FY28 $16.5B (src 15) blends 0.25/0.75 to ~$15.8B. Less ~5% for AV opex drag, consistent with my EPS haircut. Q2'26 adj. EBITDA was $2.8B, +33% (src 1).

NTM peer median ~9.4x (10 peers, core 7 ~8.5x) on the consistent MarketScreener basis (src 15). UBER today is 11.1x. I use the median with no premium: the brief requires a premium to be shown to persist, and the AV terminal risk prevents that, even though Uber's growth exceeds BKNG/EXPE/TCOM. [Citation gate 2026-10-07] [Citation gate 2026-10-07] Peer medians cited here are superseded by filings-based values: P/E 16.6x (core-7 13.3x), EV/EBITDA 9.2x (core-7 7.9x, range 4.8x TCOM to 18.6x MELI); UBER 16.7x P/E and 11.3x EV/EBITDA at the $69.48 Oct-5 close. The multiple chosen here is the agent's judgment and is unchanged.

Consensus shows net debt of ~$2.5B FY26 moving to net cash in FY27 (src 15). The Q2 release shows long-term debt of ~$10.7B against cash plus listed equity stakes (src 1). DH closes 2H27 (src 7) with ~EUR14bn bridge debt. I treat DH as EV-neutral at horizon (debt offset by acquired EBITDA) and exclude it.

bear.story: Waymo/Tesla scaling (Waymo's own app in Austin/Atlanta Jan 2028, and Waymo with Lyft in Nashville) leads the market to price permanent loss of the US Mobility profit pool before the 2028 dates arrive. Bookings slow to low-mid teens, layoff savings are fully consumed by price cuts, the AV P&L drag is sized large, and DH leverage nears 2x. ~11.5x on ~$4.3, ~6.5x NTM EV/EBITDA, a LYFT-like multiple.

base.story: High-teens bookings growth, ~25% EPS growth, buybacks resume, and DH tender clears with closing in 2H27. The multiple stays roughly where it is (~16.5x on $4.70; EV/EBITDA near the peer median), so the return comes from EPS compounding plus buybacks, not re-rating.

bull.story: AV partner cities show category growth on Uber, layoffs and CA insurance savings support margins, DH synergies are credible (high-single-digit accretion by year 3, src 7), and the P/E moves to the ~20x all-peer median on ~$5.0.

thesis_break_reason: Unchanged at $52: ~11x my NTM EPS, ~6.5x NTM EV/EBITDA, about Lyft's NTM EV/EBITDA. At that level the market would be pricing (a) bookings growth breaking toward ~10%, e.g. AV operators visibly taking US Mobility share in core metros before their 2028 dates, (b) the AV program turning into recurring losses or fleet ownership on the balance sheet, or (c) DH derailing or leverage going well above the 2x gross target (src 7). Ordinary 35%-vol moves from $70 rarely reach it without such news; the 52-week low of $65.41 was only volatility.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor confirmed my primary-document inputs: Q2'26 GB $58.0B (+22% cc), non-GAAP EPS $0.81, TTM FCF >$10B, 2.05B diluted shares, the Q3 guide, the CEO Form 4 ($10.0M at $70.96) and the $14.8B DH equity value. It corrected two things. (1) My comps: the 26x P/E and 27.8x EV/EBITDA medians were mixed-basis/trailing. On a consistent NTM basis the medians are ~19.6x P/E (core ~18x) and ~9.4x EV/EBITDA, and UBER is at 16.6x / 11.1x, roughly fairly valued. (2) DH stake: Uber's own interest is ~24.8% direct + ~11.7% derivatives, and ~53% only counting Prosus's tender (verified in the 8-K, src 7). I also drop the unverified 'first buy since 2022'. In response I kept 18x P/E (the core median, applied to EPS ~14% below consensus). I raised the FCF required yield from 7% to 7.5%, today's forward yield, because 7% on horizon-year FCF double-counted growth with a re-rate. I added an EV/EBITDA leg at the 9.5x peer median ($72). Fair value falls from $84 to ~$79.5. New primary-lane evidence: the CEO's Sep 10 Goldman keynote said 'our stock is really cheap', on the day of his buy. A 3,300-job (~10%) corporate cut was announced Sep 2, with savings to be reinvested in price (src 16,17), so I treat it as EPS-neutral with a small upside option. Consensus FY27/FY28 EPS of $4.53/$5.79 sits above my $4.15/$4.98 (src 15). Scenarios: bear $50 (25%), base $78 (50%), bull $100 (25%); mean ~$76.5. A lognormal mixture (sd 0.22-0.25), with tails widened slightly, gives P(>=$70) ~0.60 and median ~$76.5. Without re-rating, upside rests on ~25% EPS compounding plus a ~3-4% share count decline. Where I differ from the supervisor: I keep the P/E leg at 18x rather than 17.5x because my EPS is already haircut below consensus. My fair value lands close to its $79 but comes from different legs. Research limits: Uber IR events page did not render dates, and peer NTM multiples come from MarketScreener via the supervisor's rebuild plus my UBER spot check.
